correctness.rationale: The frozen mathematics is correct. In the orthonormal biased coordinate basis the affine kernel is 1 plus the sum of the normalized coordinate products. The i-th term in an evaluation row has law C_i/s_i−1, with s_i the probability of that evaluation bit and C_i independent Bernoulli(s_i). Conditioning on the other terms reduces rare-row maximization and rare-probability monotonicity to (1−s)|a|+s|a+1/s|, a nonincreasing function of s. Kernel symmetry yields weighted endpoint duality, and choosing row signs attains the bound. At the unbiased values of the other n−1 probabilities the conditioning variable a takes −1 (even n) or −2 (odd n≥3) with positive probability, giving the strict fair minimum when one probability changes, and monotonicity handles the rest. The mean-one kernel variable is bounded below by −(n−1), strictly above that on a positive-probability success event; its negative part tends in expectation to n−1 as all rare probabilities tend to zero. The corrected claim uses the established formula only as a premise. In four coordinates with p_i≤1/2, no outcome with at least two successes contributes a negative part. Splitting zero and one success gives the corrected closed expression. Exact evaluation gives 77/27, 371/128 and 6213/2048, with signed gaps 161/3456 and 277/2048, and both nonconstant vectors majorize the constant vector of the same sum. Hence the repaired non-Schur assertion follows. The corrected scientific notes match the retained verification code and the frozen JSON front matter is preserved.
residual_risks: The independent rational reconstruction checks weighted rows and columns for six examples, including all three repaired witnesses; it does not establish an all-dimensional extremum theorem. No formal verification or expert attestation is claimed.

value.rationale: The repaired result answers a natural optimization question about averaging coordinate biases while keeping the expected total number of successes fixed. It supplies explicit witnesses to both failures of ordering, and the change of sign of the one-success residual explains why the familiar product-maximization argument need not survive beyond the threshold. This is a motivated negative result with consequences for bias-balancing heuristics, not novelty attributed to individual computed constants or a covered headline.
